declared_limit.rationale: Kept and proved by the reviewer's probe: WatchdogTest AC-6 (awaitQueued(0)) and AC-4 (no naruserve-proxy*watchdog* thread alive) read JVM-global ProxyExchange.Scheduler.INSTANCE state, and :NaruServe-proxy:test runs every class in one JVM (root build.gradle only sets forkEvery=1 on NaruServe-tinyhttpd's isolatedTest; the proxy project has no forkEvery or maxParallelForks). It does not cause spurious failures in this repository's test runs, because no other test leaves a reservation pending. Outside WatchdogTest, no test class arms Scheduler.INSTANCE directly; the only custom watchdog, ProxyExchangeTest's RecordingWatchdog, is injected through withWatchdog and is not the singleton. Every un-awaited-looking submit (ProxyCheckOrderTest:259, ProxyConcurrencyTest pending lists, ProxyExchangeTest:330/541, ProxyMethodTest:209, ProxyRequestTargetTest:279) is awaited or released inside the test, or by @After (releaseAll / hold.countDown / app.shutdown(2s) / closeables.close()), so in-flight requests end and cancel their reservation before the next class runs. WatchdogTest's own direct reservations (lines 279, 449-450) are 100-400 ms and are released. Write deadlines and TLS handshake deadlines are disarmed in finally. Anything still settling is absorbed by awaitQueued's 5 s poll after 1000 requests and by AC-4's 30 s wait. A pending 5-minute reservation can only come from an earlier test that has already failed or timed out (a cascading secondary failure on a run that is already red) or from the reviewer's synthetic probe. Not blocking; record it, and fix it when a test that can leak is added (baseline-relative queue count, fresh-JVM idle-thread check).
declared_limit.evidence: Reviewer probe ReviewProbeOrderTest (one 5-minute reservation armed on Scheduler.INSTANCE before running WatchdogTest AC-6 via JUnitCore) -> 'reservations in the scheduler queue expected:<0> but was:<1>'. Classifier check: grep of NaruServe-proxy/src/test for Scheduler.INSTANCE / .watch( / reserve( finds only WatchdogTest (short, released) and ProxyExchangeTest's RecordingWatchdog; build.gradle:341-347 (no forkEvery for :NaruServe-proxy), build.gradle:366-377 (forkEvery only on tinyhttpd isolatedTest); @After teardowns of ProxyConcurrencyTest/ProxyTimeoutsTest/ProxyLifetimeSocketTest/ProxyMidResponseFailureTest/ProxyRequestBodyTest release held backends and shut apps down.

rejected.rationale: Naming only. The AC-6 test reuses the app(http, https) helper and puts a plain-HTTP silent backend on the /https mount. The request still holds a reservation as AC-6 intends, so behaviour and AC coverage are unaffected.

Intended design. Proxy's package-private watchdog constructor/withWatchdog is a test seam (REL-PROXY-001). Every public Proxy.to path uses ProxyExchange.Scheduler.INSTANCE, so the TLS handshake deadline that TlsConnector arms on Scheduler.INSTANCE always shares the one JVM-wide scheduler, as REL-PROXY-002 requires. The reviewer dropped it too.

clean_code_triage.reason: Valid DRY finding with a principle and an exact location (Proxy.java Options constructor, about lines 966-981). The response-rule branch repeats the value/removal split that valueRules() already does: fixedResponseHeaders can come from valueRules(resolved), and the hidden lower-case names from a small removal-names helper. Proxy.java is in the lane write set, and the change preserves behaviour.
Building both sets from one forwarding-name list in HeaderRules means editing HeaderRules.java, which is outside the lane write set.
Extracting an IpLiterals helper means creating a new IpLiterals.java, which is outside the lane write set. The IP literal check serves only the backend head builder for SEC-PROXY-002.

Conflicts with a project convention. The module deliberately keeps package-private test accessors in main code (Proxy.java:300 'Package-private accessors: the configured values, read by unit tests only (D-046)', plus the existing withWatchdog test seam). executorIfCreated/queuedReservations/watchdog() follow that pattern and are documented with @req REL-PROXY-002.

Moving the fakes to shared test fixtures means new or changed files outside the lane write set (for example RawBackend.java or a new fixtures class). The size comes from one class per requirement covering AC-1..AC-7, which is the module's existing test-class convention, and no specific defect is named.
